tex_content.html:
egin{exercise} \end{exercise} 1. ch4:4.20Suppose $F$ is a smooth $(k,l)$-tensor field and $G$ is a smooth $(r,s)$-tensor field. Show that the components of the total covariant derivative of $F \otimes G$ are given by \[ ( abla (F \otimes G))^{j_1\cdots j_k p_1\cdots p_r}_{i_1\cdots i_l q_1\cdots q_s;m} = F^{j_1\cdots j_k}_{i_1\cdots i_l;m} G^{p_1\cdots p_r}_{q_1\cdots q_s} + F^{j_1\cdots j_k}_{i_1\cdots i_l} G^{p_1\cdots p_r}_{q_1\cdots q_s;m}. \]

[Remark: This formula is often written in the following way, more suggestive of the product rule for ordinary derivatives: \[ \left(F^{j_1\cdots j_k}_{i_1\cdots i_l} G^{p_1\cdots p_r}_{q_1\cdots q_s} ight)_{;m} = F^{j_1\cdots j_k}_{i_1\cdots i_l;m} G^{p_1\cdots p_r}_{q_1\cdots q_s} + F^{j_1\cdots j_k}_{i_1\cdots i_l} G^{p_1\cdots p_r}_{q_1\cdots q_s;m}. \]

Notice that this does not say that $ abla (F \otimes G) = ( abla F) \otimes G + F \otimes ( abla G)$, because in the first term on the right-hand side of this latter formula, the index resulting from differentiation is not the last lower index.] \end{exercise}
